fullPassage: The debate over the basis of law, a central issue in both legal philosophy and ethical theory, is between two main concepts: positive law and natural law. According to positive law supporters, law is only valid when it is officially written down, and once in text form, it should be obeyed, regardless of its moral correctness. Additionally, since people do not always share the same moral values, different laws can be made about the same practices, such as euthanasia, at different moments in history and across different countries. But the advocates of natural law contend that if a written law contradicts certain moral principles, it should be considered unjust. Martin Luther King Jr. once said people should disobey man-made laws that go against natural law, which aligns with Aristotle’s view that “natural justice is everywhere,” suggesting natural law transcends human legislation. As such, natural law is not dependent on any group of people. What is moral and immoral exists in nature, and humans discover it by making decisions that accord with their intrinsic understanding of right and wrong. This sense is universal and is consistent throughout time and space.

questions.passage: The debate over the basis of law, a central issue in both legal philosophy and ethical theory, is between two main concepts: positive law and natural law. According to positive law supporters, law is only valid when it is officially written down, and once in text form, it should be obeyed, regardless of its moral correctness. Additionally, since people do not always <u>share</u> the same moral values, different laws can be made about the same practices, such as euthanasia, at different moments in history and across different countries. But the advocates of natural law contend that if a written law contradicts certain moral principles, it should be considered unjust. Martin Luther King Jr. once said people should disobey man-made laws that go against natural law, which aligns with Aristotle’s view that “natural justice is everywhere,” suggesting natural law transcends human legislation. As such, natural law is not dependent on any group of people. This sense is universal and is consistent throughout time and space.

questions.passage: According to positive law supporters, law is only valid when it is officially written down, and once in text form, it should be __________ (obey), regardless of its moral correctness.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: should be 뒤에는 과거분사가 와야 하므로 obey를 obeyed로 바꿔 수동태를 만듦
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞에 조동사 + be동사(should be)가 있어요. 법은 사람들에 의해 '지켜지는' 대상이므로 수동태(be + 과거분사)가 필요해요. 그래서 obey를 과거분사 obeyed로 바꿔요
→ it should be obeyed(그것은 지켜져야 한다)
동사원형 obey를 그대로 두면 be동사 뒤에 동사원형이 와서 문법상 성립하지 않아요
det.tip: should be + 과거분사(p.p.) = 수동태. obey → obeyed

questions.passage: But the advocates of natural law contend that if a written law contradicts certain moral principles, it should be __________ (consider) unjust.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: should be 뒤 과거분사 자리이므로 consider를 considered로 바꿔 수동태를 만듦
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞의 should be로 보아 수동태(be + 과거분사)가 필요해요. 그런 법은 사람들에 의해 부당하다고 '여겨지는' 대상이므로 consider를 과거분사 considered로 바꿔요
→ it should be considered unjust(그것은 부당하다고 여겨져야 한다)
여기서 unjust는 '부당한'이라는 형용사 보어예요. consider A B(A를 B로 여기다)가 수동이 되면 A be considered B가 돼요
det.tip: should be + 과거분사 = 수동태. consider → considered

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: intrinsic understanding of right and wrong=옳고 그름에 대한 내재적 이해
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장은 '인간은 자신의 ____에 부합하는 결정을 내림으로써 도덕을 발견한다'는 자연법의 핵심이에요. 도덕은 밖이 아니라 인간 내면에 있는 옳고 그름의 감각으로 찾는 것이므로 intrinsic understanding of right and wrong(옳고 그름에 대한 내재적 이해)이 적절
① strict obedience to written rules(성문 규칙에 대한 엄격한 복종) — 실정법 논리라 자연법 문맥과 반대
② official approval by the government(정부의 공식 승인) — 특정 집단에 의존하지 않는다는 흐름과 모순
③ intrinsic understanding of right and wrong(옳고 그름에 대한 내재적 이해) ✅ 정답 — 내면의 도덕 감각으로 도덕을 발견함
④ financial reward for their effort(노력에 대한 금전적 보상) — 도덕 판단과 무관
det.tip: 도덕은 인간 내면의 옳고 그름 감각으로 발견 → intrinsic understanding of right and wrong

ch: intrinsic understanding of right and wrong
